human_tolerance.notes: The most familiar woodpecker in North American towns: it works lawns and flowerbeds for ants, and will nest in a post or a suitably sized birdhouse as readily as in a tree.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Nesting in a cavity; nestlings cling to the cavity wall from about 17 days old and fledge 25 to 28 days after hatching.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Those birds that migrate leave the northern breeding grounds from September and October and return from the beginning of April; the winter diet of the birds that stay shifts to berries and seeds, including poison ivy, dogwood, sumac and wild cherry.

vocalizations.description: A sustained laugh, ki ki ki ki, flat at first and then rising into a loud noise; several of these names derive from attempts to imitate it. Given on the ground, from a snag and in flight.
The same ki ki ki ki given as a territorial signal toward a rival, and a sharper version when a nestling or an adult is flushed from the cavity.

range.note: Country list reduced from the article's range description: breeds in Canada and the United States and resident in Mexico, with northern populations withdrawing south in winter.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: A woodpecker that climbs trunks and braces with its tail, walks and hops over open ground foraging for ants, and flies between feeding and nest sites; the split between climbing and ground foraging is a judgement.

traits.nest_type.note: 'It is a cavity nester that typically nests in trees, but may also use posts and birdhouses if sized and situated appropriately'; the entrance hole is about 8 cm across and the cavity 33-41 cm deep.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of 'The body mass can vary from 86 to 167 g'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The oldest yet known yellow-shafted northern flicker lived to be at least 9 years 2 months old', and a six-year capture-mark-recapture study found only one to two birds in every 300 adults were 7 or more years old. No mean is given, so 2.0 years is a judgement reflecting that very low adult survival, not a sourced mean.

traits.diet.note: 'their primary food is insects. Ants alone can make up 45% of their diet', with berries and seeds taken especially in winter. Shares are a judgement that puts ants and other invertebrates clearly first.

traits.social.note: Flickers are largely solitary and territorial in the breeding season and forage singly or in small family groups; the article's territorial call exchange implies pairs holding ground.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'especially active on warm days' is stated for a related ground squirrel, not here; for the flicker, foraging by day and roosting in cavities by night follows from its cavity-roosting behaviour and its ant-foraging in open ground.

traits.defense.note: 'The common predators are Cooper's hawks, sharp-shinned hawks, common raccoons, squirrels, and snakes'; a woodpecker under threat flies off rather than confronting, and nestlings are described as helpless.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: it feeds on open lawns and in gardens and will nest in birdhouses, so it tolerates people well.

habitat.use.note: 'The northern flicker may be observed in open habitats near trees, including woodlands, edges, yards, and parks', and it forages on the ground for ants; a roughly even split between tree time and ground time is a judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: 'the species' propensity for roosting in cavities' - 'cavity' is the matching drawable shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Insect-dominated diet with winter berries and seeds, cavity nesting and cavity roosting; the ant foraging on open ground links it to leaf litter and bare soil. Weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Yards, parks and birdhouses are named explicitly.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Northern flickers are partial migrants, some southern populations being completely non-migratory.'

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement: some northern-breeding birds withdraw south, but many winter well north of the breeding range, so roughly half the population stays.

seasonal.phases.note: The article gives nestling and fledging ages and an autumn return migration 'between September and October' but no calendar window for laying; the breeding and wintering windows here are a judgement placed on the Great Plains breeding season.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Young fly at 25 to 28 days after hatching', and nestlings cling to the cavity wall from about 17 days old; 28 days is the upper end of the sourced fledging age and the 0.85 scale is a judgement.

vocalizations.laugh.note: 'This bird's call is a sustained laugh, ki ki ki ki'; 'the calls' pattern can be classified as flat and gradually rises into a loud noise.'

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'If the call is used towards a male, it is a territorial sign' and 'juvenile northern flickers are often helpless against predators who enter the nest'; the separate alarm call here is the same laugh used defensively, which is a judgement.

look.note: Brown-and-tan barred body with a black bib and moustachial stripe, a red crescent on the nape and a dark, long, chisel-shaped bill; palette and proportions are judgement, and the nape crescent is drawn as a small extra part so the red shows.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program, with the sustained laugh standing in for song and insects as the food tag.
